slot.brief: Given path difference (or position on screen with d, D), convert to phase difference and find I/I_max at that point.

stem: In a Young's double slit experiment, the slits are $0.6$ mm apart and the screen is $1.2$ m away. The wavelength of light used is $600$ nm. The intensity at a point $0.3$ mm from the central bright fringe, in terms of the maximum intensity $I_0$, is

verdicts.working: Fringe width: β = λD/d = (600×10⁻⁹)(1.2)/(0.6×10⁻³) = 1.2 mm. At y = 0.3 mm = β/4, I/I₀ = cos²(πy/β) = cos²(π/4) = 1/2.

working:
Path difference $\Delta x = \dfrac{yd}{D} = \dfrac{0.3 \times 10^{-3} \times 0.6 \times 10^{-3}}{1.2} = 1.5 \times 10^{-7}$ m $= 150$ nm $= \dfrac{\lambda}{4}$. Phase difference $\delta = \dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda} \Delta x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$. Intensity $I = I_0 \cos^2 \dfrac{\delta}{2} = I_0 \cos^2 \dfrac{\pi}{4} = \dfrac{I_0}{2}$.

Independent check: Fringe width: β = λD/d = (600×10⁻⁹)(1.2)/(0.6×10⁻³) = 1.2 mm. At y = 0.3 mm = β/4, I/I₀ = cos²(πy/β) = cos²(π/4) = 1/2.
solution: The path difference is $\Delta x=\dfrac{yd}{D}=\dfrac{(0.3\times10^{-3})(0.6\times10^{-3})}{1.2}=150\,\text{nm}=\dfrac{\lambda}{4}$, so the phase difference is $\delta=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.\n$$I=I_0\cos^2\left(\dfrac{\delta}{2}\right)=I_0\cos^2\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)=\dfrac{I_0}{2}.$$
